rows.stem: Solid Calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to form Calcium hydroxide accompanied by the liberation of heat. From the information given above it may be concluded that this reaction

options.label: A
options.text: is endothermic and pH of the solution formed is more than 7.

options.label: B
options.text: is exothermic and pH of the solution formed is 7.

options.label: C
options.text: is endothermic and pH of the solution formed is 7.

options.label: D
options.text: is exothermic and pH of the solution formed is more than 7.

rows.solution:
Calcium oxide combines with water to form calcium hydroxide, and the reaction gives out a lot of heat, so it is exothermic:

\(\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq)}\) + heat

Calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) is a base, so its solution has a pH more than 7.

This is option (D) is exothermic and pH of the solution formed is more than 7.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: Juice of tamarind turns blue litmus to red. It is because of the presence of an acid called :
rows.solution:
Tamarind contains tartaric acid, which turns blue litmus red. (Methanoic acid is in ant and nettle stings, acetic acid in vinegar, and oxalic acid in tomato.)

This is option (C) tartaric acid.

rows.stem: Select from the following a process in which a combination reaction is involved :
rows.solution:
Coal is mainly carbon. When it burns, carbon combines with oxygen to form a single product, carbon dioxide:

\(\mathrm{C(s) + O_2(g) \rightarrow CO_2(g)}\)

Two substances giving one product is a combination reaction. Burning methane gives two products (carbon dioxide and water), black and white photography uses the decomposition of silver bromide, and digestion breaks food down.

This is option (B) Burning of coal.

rows.stem: The oxide which can react with \(\mathrm{HCl}\) as well as \(\mathrm{KOH}\) to give corresponding salt and water is
rows.solution:
An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases to give a salt and water is amphoteric. Aluminium oxide is amphoteric:

\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 6HCl \rightarrow 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2O}\)

\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 2KOH \rightarrow 2KAlO_2 + H_2O}\)

Copper oxide, sodium oxide and potassium oxide are basic oxides and react only with acids.

This is option (B) \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\).

rows.stem:
Consider the following cases :

(a) \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 + Al} \longrightarrow\)

(b) \(\mathrm{CuSO_4 + Ca} \longrightarrow\)

(c) \(\mathrm{FeSO_4 + Cu} \longrightarrow\)

(d) \(\mathrm{ZnSO_4 + Mg} \longrightarrow\)

The cases in which new products will form are –
rows.solution:
A metal displaces another metal from its salt solution only if it is more reactive.

(a) Calcium is more reactive than aluminium, so aluminium cannot displace it: no reaction.

(b) Calcium is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper: new products form.

(c) Copper is less reactive than iron: no reaction.

(d) Magnesium is more reactive than zinc, so it displaces zinc: new products form.

So new products form in (b) and (d). This is option (D).

rows.stem:
Identify the correct statement about the following reaction :

\(\mathrm{2H_2S + SO_2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{2H_2O + S}\)

options.label: A
options.text: \(\mathrm{H_2S}\) is oxidising agent and \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) is reducing agent.

options.label: C
options.text: \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) is oxidising agent and \(\mathrm{H_2S}\) is reducing agent.

rows.solution:
\(\mathrm{H_2S}\) loses hydrogen and becomes sulphur, so it is oxidised; it is the reducing agent. \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) loses oxygen and becomes sulphur, so it is reduced; it is the oxidising agent.

This is option (C) \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) is oxidising agent and \(\mathrm{H_2S}\) is reducing agent.

rows.stem:
Consider the following statements about homologous series of carbon compounds :

(a) All succeeding members differ by \(-\mathrm{CH_2}\) unit.

(b) Melting point and boiling point increases with increasing molecular mass.

(c) The difference in molecular masses between two successive members is 16 u.

(d) \(\mathrm{C_2H_2}\) and \(\mathrm{C_3H_4}\) are **NOT** the successive members of alkyne series.

The correct statements are –
rows.solution:
(a) Successive members of a homologous series differ by a \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) unit: true.

(b) Melting and boiling points rise as the molecular mass increases: true.

(c) The difference in molecular mass between successive members is that of \(\mathrm{CH_2}\), \(12 + 2 = 14\) u, not 16 u: false.

(d) \(\mathrm{C_2H_2}\) (ethyne) and \(\mathrm{C_3H_4}\) (propyne) are successive members of the alkyne series, so the statement that they are not is false.

So statements (a) and (b) are the correct ones. This is option (A).

rows.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is (are) \(\underline{\text{true}}\) about human heart ?

(a) Right atrium receives oxygenated blood from lungs through pulmonary artery.

(b) Left atrium transfers oxygenated blood to left ventricle which sends it to various parts of the body.

(c) Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood through vena cava from upper and lower body.

(d) Left atrium transfers oxygenated blood to aorta which sends it to different parts of the body.
rows.solution:
(a) is false: oxygenated blood from the lungs comes to the left atrium through the pulmonary vein, not to the right atrium through the pulmonary artery.

(b) is true: the left atrium passes oxygenated blood to the left ventricle, which pumps it to the body.

(c) is true: the right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the upper and lower body through the vena cava.

(d) is false: it is the left ventricle, not the left atrium, that pumps blood into the aorta.

So statements (b) and (c) are true. This is option (C).

rows.stem: Select out of the following a gland which does **NOT** occur as a pair in the human body :
rows.solution:
The pituitary gland is a single gland at the base of the brain. Ovaries, testes and adrenal glands all occur in pairs.

This is option (A) Pituitary.

rows.stem: In human respiratory system, when a person breathes in, the position of ribs and diaphragm will be :

options.label: A
options.text: lifted ribs and curve/dome shaped diaphragm.

options.label: D
options.text: relaxed ribs and curve/dome shaped diaphragm.

rows.solution:
When we breathe in, the rib muscles lift the ribs and the diaphragm contracts and flattens. This enlarges the chest cavity, and air is sucked into the lungs.

This is option (B) lifted ribs and flattened diaphragm.

rows.stem: Identify the mode of asexual reproduction in the following organism :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the organism exists only as a drawing (a small tentacled organism); the stem names nothing, and naming it here would state the answer. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
The drawing shows a small organism (Hydra) with an outgrowth developing on the side of its body. Such a bud forms by repeated cell division at one specific site, grows into a tiny individual and, when mature, detaches from the parent.

This is option (C) Budding.

rows.stem: A cross made between two pea plants produces 50% tall and 50% short pea plants. The gene combination of the parental pea plants must be
rows.solution:
A cross of Tt with tt gives gametes T and t from the first parent and only t from the second:

Tt \(\times\) tt gives Tt : tt \(= 1 : 1\), that is 50% tall (Tt) and 50% short (tt).

(The crosses TT with Tt and TT with tt give only tall plants, and Tt with Tt gives tall and short in the ratio 3 : 1.)

This is option (C) Tt and tt.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
Consider the following statements in the context of human eye :

(a) The diameter of the eye ball is about 2.3 cm.

(b) Iris is a dark muscular diaphragm that controls the size of the pupil.

(c) Most of the refraction for the light rays entering the eye occurs at the crystalline lens.

(d) While focusing on the objects at different distances the distance between the crystalline lens and the retina is adjusted by ciliary muscles.

The correct statements are –
rows.solution:
(a) The diameter of the eyeball is about 2.3 cm: true.

(b) The iris is a dark muscular diaphragm that controls the size of the pupil: true.

(c) Most of the refraction of light entering the eye happens at the outer surface of the cornea, not at the crystalline lens: false.

(d) The distance between the lens and the retina is fixed; the ciliary muscles change the curvature, and so the focal length, of the lens: false.

So statements (a) and (b) are true. This is option (A).

rows.stem: The maximum resistance of a network of five identical resistors of \(\frac{1}{5}\,\Omega\) each can be –
rows.solution:
Resistance is greatest when all five resistors are joined in series:

\(R = 5 \times \dfrac{1}{5} = 1\,\Omega\).

This is option (A) \(1\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: Study the I-V graph for three resistors of resistances \(\mathrm{R_1}\), \(\mathrm{R_2}\) and \(\mathrm{R_3}\) and select the correct statement from the following :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the I-V graph (I in ampere on the vertical axis, V in volts on the horizontal axis, three straight lines from the origin labelled R1, R2 and R3) is the only source of the comparison; which line is steepest is withheld here because it is the answer. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
In an I-V graph the slope of each line is \(\dfrac{I}{V} = \dfrac{1}{R}\), so the steeper the line, the smaller the resistance. The line for \(\mathrm{R_1}\) is the steepest and the line for \(\mathrm{R_3}\) the least steep, so \(\mathrm{R_1}\) is the smallest resistance and \(\mathrm{R_3}\) the largest.

This is option (C) \(\mathrm{R_3 > R_2 > R_1}\).

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: Strength of magnetic field produced by a current carrying solenoid **DOES NOT** depend upon :

options.label: A
options.text: number of turns in the solenoid

options.label: B
options.text: direction of the current flowing through it

options.label: D
options.text: material of core of the solenoid

rows.solution:
The strength of the field of a solenoid depends on the number of turns, the current, the radius and the material of the core. Reversing the direction of the current only reverses the direction of the field; its strength stays the same.

This is option (B) direction of the current flowing through it.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Different metals have different reactivities with water and dilute acids.

**Reason (R) :** Extraction of a metal from its ore depends on its position in the reactivity series.
rows.context: These questions consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Different metals react with water and dilute acids with different vigour (potassium violently, iron slowly, copper not at all), so the Assertion is true. The method used to extract a metal does depend on its position in the reactivity series, so the Reason is also true.

But the Reason is about extraction; it does not explain why reactivities differ. Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Human female has a perfect pair of sex chromosome.

**Reason (R) :** Sex chromosome contributed by the human male in the zygote decides the sex of a child.
rows.context: These questions consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
A human female has two X chromosomes, a perfect (matched) pair, so the Assertion is true. The mother always gives an X chromosome, while the father gives either X or Y, so the chromosome from the father decides the sex of the child. The Reason is true.

But the Reason explains how the sex of the child is decided, not why the female's pair is perfect. Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Myopic eye cannot see distant objects distinctly.

**Reason (R) :** For the correction of myopia converging lenses of appropriate power are prescribed by eye-surgeons.
rows.context: These questions consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
In a myopic eye the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina, so distant objects are not seen distinctly. The Assertion is true.

Myopia is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens of suitable power, not a converging lens, so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The deflection of a compass needle placed near a current carrying wire decreases when the magnitude of an electric current in the wire is increased.

**Reason (R) :** Strength of the magnetic field at a point due to a current carrying conductor increases on increasing the current in the conductor.
rows.context: These questions consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Increasing the current in the wire increases the strength of its magnetic field, so the deflection of the compass needle increases, not decreases. The Assertion is false.

The field at a point due to a current-carrying conductor does increase with the current, so the Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem: “No precipitation reaction can occur without exchange of ions between the two reactants.” Justify this statement giving a balanced chemical equation for the reaction.
rows.solution:
A precipitation reaction is a double displacement reaction: the ions of the two reactants exchange partners, and one of the new combinations is insoluble and separates out as a precipitate. The insoluble product exists only because of this exchange of ions, so no precipitate can form without it.

Example: sodium sulphate and barium chloride exchange ions to give a white precipitate of barium sulphate:

\(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4(aq) + BaCl_2(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}\)

rows.stem: Giving one example of each, differentiate between a displacement reaction and a double displacement reaction.
rows.solution:
In a displacement reaction a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution; there is no exchange of ions between the two reactants. Example:

\(\mathrm{Fe(s) + CuSO_4(aq) \rightarrow FeSO_4(aq) + Cu(s)}\)

In a double displacement reaction the two reactants exchange ions. Example:

\(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4(aq) + BaCl_2(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}\)

rows.stem: Photosynthesis takes place in the leaves and the food prepared by it reaches other parts of the plants. Name the process involved and explain it.
rows.solution:
The process is translocation.

The soluble products of photosynthesis (food such as sucrose) are carried from the leaves to other parts of the plant through the phloem, in the sieve tubes, with the help of the companion cells. The movement takes place both upwards and downwards. It uses energy from ATP: sucrose is moved into the phloem, which raises the osmotic pressure there, water enters, and the pressure pushes the food to the parts where it is needed.

rows.stem: “Stability of DNA in a species is ensured during sexual reproduction.” Justify the statement.
rows.solution:
Each germ cell receives only one chromosome from each pair (of either maternal or paternal origin), so it has half the number of chromosomes of a body cell.

When two germ cells from the two parents fuse at fertilisation, the original number of chromosomes is restored in the progeny. So the number of chromosomes, and the amount of DNA, stays the same from generation to generation, which ensures the stability of DNA of the species.

rows.stem: State two laws of refraction of light.
rows.solution:
(i) The incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal to the interface of the two transparent media at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.

(ii) For light of a given colour and a given pair of media, the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is a constant (Snell's law):

\(\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \text{constant}\).

The law must be stated in words, not only as the ratio.

rows.stem: Define the term absolute refractive index of a medium. A ray of light enters from vacuum to glass of absolute refractive index 1.5. Find the speed of light in glass. The speed of light in vacuum is \(3 \times 10^8\) m/s.
rows.solution:
The absolute refractive index of a medium is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum (or air) to the speed of light in that medium: \(n_m = \dfrac{c}{v_m}\).

Here \(c = 3 \times 10^8\) m/s and \(n_m = 1.5\), so

\(v_m = \dfrac{c}{n_m} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5} = 2 \times 10^8\) m/s.

rows.stem: Use Ohm’s law to determine the potential difference across the \(3\,\Omega\) resistor in the circuit shown in the following diagram when key is closed :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit (key K, a 2 V cell, and resistors of 1 Ω, 2 Ω and 3 Ω in one series loop) is given only as a drawing; the stem names only the 3 Ω resistor. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
The key, the 2 V cell and the three resistors are all in one series loop, so

\(R_s = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6\,\Omega\).

By Ohm's law the current is \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}\) A, and the same current flows through every resistor.

Potential difference across the \(3\,\Omega\) resistor: \(V = IR = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 3 = 1\) V.

rows.stem: Name the term used for the materials which **cannot** be broken down by biological processes. Give two ways by which they harm various components of an ecosystem.
rows.solution:
Such materials are called non-biodegradable substances.

Any two ways in which they harm the ecosystem: they are inert and persist in the environment for a long time, causing pollution; they enter food chains and accumulate at higher trophic levels (biological magnification); they reduce the fertility of the soil.

rows.stem: It is observed that Calcium on reaction with water floats on its surface. Explain why it happens. Also write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction that occurs. What happens when the aqueous solution of the product of this reaction reacts with Carbon dioxide gas ? Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction.
rows.solution:
Calcium reacts with water less vigorously than sodium. The bubbles of hydrogen gas formed stick to the surface of the calcium and make it lighter than water, so it floats.

\(\mathrm{Ca(s) + 2H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq) + H_2(g)}\)

When carbon dioxide is passed through the calcium hydroxide solution (lime water), it turns milky because insoluble calcium carbonate forms:

\(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2(aq) + CO_2(g) \rightarrow CaCO_3(s) + H_2O(l)}\)

rows.stem: Draw a labelled diagram to show electrolytic refining of copper. State what happens when electric current is passed through the electrolyte taken in this case.
rows.solution:
Diagram: draw a tank containing acidified copper sulphate solution (the electrolyte). Dip a thick block of impure copper into it as the anode, connected to the positive terminal of a battery, and a thin strip of pure copper as the cathode, connected to the negative terminal, with a key in the circuit. Show the impurities settling at the bottom below the anode as anode mud. Label the anode, the cathode and the electrolyte.

When current is passed, copper from the impure anode dissolves into the electrolyte as \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) ions, and an equivalent amount of pure copper from the solution is deposited on the cathode:

At the anode: \(\mathrm{Cu \rightarrow Cu^{2+} + 2e^-}\)

At the cathode: \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Cu}\)

Soluble impurities go into the solution, and insoluble ones settle below the anode as anode mud.

rows.stem:
Give reasons for the following :

(i) Alveoli in lungs are richly supplied with blood capillaries.

(ii) Respiratory pigment in the blood takes up oxygen and not carbon dioxide.

(iii) During anaerobic respiration, a 3-carbon molecule is formed as an end product instead of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) in human beings.
rows.solution:
(i) The alveoli are where oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out. A rich supply of blood capillaries gives a large surface in close contact with the air, so the exchange of gases is efficient.

(ii) The respiratory pigment, haemoglobin, has a very high affinity for oxygen, so it takes up oxygen in the lungs. Carbon dioxide is more soluble in water and is mostly carried dissolved in the blood plasma.

(iii) During vigorous activity the muscle cells run short of oxygen, so glucose is not oxidised completely to carbon dioxide and water. Instead pyruvate is converted into lactic acid, a 3-carbon molecule.

rows.stem:
(i) Name the movements that occur all along the gut in human digestive system. How do they help in digestion ?

(ii) Where is bile juice stored in human body ? List two roles of bile juice.
rows.solution:
(i) Peristaltic movements (peristalsis). The muscles of the gut wall contract rhythmically to push the food forward in a regulated manner, so that each part of the gut processes it properly and it is digested.

(ii) Bile juice is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder.

Two roles: it breaks large fat globules into smaller ones (emulsification of fats), which makes the action of enzymes easier; and it makes the acidic food coming from the stomach alkaline, so that the pancreatic enzymes can act.

rows.stem: Explain the events that take place once a sperm reaches the oviduct till it becomes a foetus. Write the role of placenta in pregnancy.
rows.solution:
In the oviduct the sperm meets the egg and fertilisation takes place, forming a zygote.

The zygote starts dividing and forms a ball of cells, the embryo. The embryo is implanted in the thick lining of the uterus, where it continues to grow and develops organs to become a foetus.

Role of the placenta: it is a disc embedded in the uterine wall with villi on the embryo's side, which provide a large surface for glucose and oxygen to pass from the mother's blood to the embryo; the wastes produced by the embryo are removed by transferring them into the mother's blood.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Define the term power of accommodation of human eye. Write the name of the part of eye which plays a major role in the process of accommodation and explain what happens when human eye focuses (i) nearby objects and (ii) distant objects.
rows.solution:
The power of accommodation is the ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length.

The ciliary muscles play the major role.

(i) For nearby objects the ciliary muscles contract, the eye lens becomes thicker and its focal length decreases.

(ii) For distant objects the ciliary muscles relax, the eye lens becomes thinner and its focal length increases.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Draw a ray diagram to show the formation of a rainbow in the sky. On this diagram mark A – where dispersion of light occurs, B – where internal reflection of light occurs and C – where refraction of light occurs. List two necessary conditions to observe a rainbow.
rows.solution:
Diagram: draw a ray of sunlight falling on a spherical raindrop. At A, where it enters the drop, it is refracted and dispersed into its colours. At B, on the back surface of the drop, the light is reflected internally. At C, where it leaves the drop, it is refracted again and the colours emerge spread out towards the observer. Mark A, B and C on these three points.

Two conditions to observe a rainbow:

1. There must be tiny water droplets in the atmosphere (as after a rain shower).

2. The sun must be behind the observer.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem: Draw a diagram to show the pattern of magnetic field lines on a horizontal sheet of paper due to a straight conductor passing through its centre and carrying current vertically upwards. Mark on it (i) the direction of current in the conductor and (ii) the corresponding magnetic field lines. State right hand thumb rule and check whether the directions marked by you are in accordance with this rule or not.
rows.solution:
Diagram: draw a horizontal sheet of cardboard with a straight wire passing vertically through its centre, connected in a circuit with a battery. (i) Mark the current in the wire with an arrow pointing upwards. (ii) Draw the field lines as concentric circles on the sheet, centred on the wire, and mark them with arrows going anticlockwise as seen from above.

Right-hand thumb rule: imagine holding the current-carrying straight conductor in the right hand with the thumb pointing in the direction of the current; the fingers then wrap around the conductor in the direction of the magnetic field lines.

Check: with the thumb pointing upwards, the fingers curl anticlockwise as seen from above, which is the direction marked on the field lines. So the directions are in accordance with the rule.

rows.stem: Use of pesticides to protect our crops affect organisms at various trophic levels especially human beings. Name the phenomenon involved and explain how does it happen.
rows.solution:
The phenomenon is biological magnification (biomagnification).

Pesticides sprayed on crops are washed down into the soil and into water bodies. From the soil they are absorbed by plants along with water and minerals, and from water bodies by aquatic plants and animals, so they enter the food chain. These chemicals are non-biodegradable, so they accumulate progressively at each trophic level. Human beings occupy the top level in any food chain, so the maximum concentration of these chemicals builds up in our bodies.

rows.stem:
(i) Give reason why carbon can neither form \(\mathrm{C^{4+}}\) cations nor \(\mathrm{C^{4-}}\) anions but form covalent compounds.

(ii) What is homologous series of carbon compound ? Write the molecular formula of any two consecutive members of homologous series of aldehydes.

(iii) Draw the structure of the molecule of cyclohexane \((\mathrm{C_6H_{12}})\).
rows.solution:
(i) Carbon has four valence electrons. It cannot form a \(\mathrm{C^{4+}}\) cation because removing four electrons would need a large amount of energy. It cannot form a \(\mathrm{C^{4-}}\) anion because it would be difficult for a nucleus with six protons to hold ten electrons. So carbon shares its valence electrons with other atoms and forms covalent compounds.

(ii) A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain; its members have similar chemical properties and successive members differ by a \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) unit.

Two consecutive aldehydes: ethanal, \(\mathrm{C_2H_4O}\) (\(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)), and propanal, \(\mathrm{C_3H_6O}\) (\(\mathrm{C_2H_5CHO}\)). (Any other pair of consecutive members is also correct.)

(iii) Cyclohexane: six carbon atoms joined by single bonds in a closed ring (a hexagon), with two hydrogen atoms attached to each carbon atom.

rows.stem:
(i) Name a commercially important carbon compound having functional group \(-\mathrm{OH}\) and write its molecular formula.

(ii) Write chemical equation to show its reaction with

(1) Sodium metal

(2) Excess conc. sulphuric acid

(3) Ethanoic acid in the presence of an acid catalyst

(4) Acidified potassium dichromate

Also write the name of the product formed in each case.
rows.solution:
(i) Ethanol, molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\).

(ii) (1) With sodium metal: sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas.

\(\mathrm{2C_2H_5OH + 2Na \rightarrow 2C_2H_5ONa + H_2}\)

(2) Heated at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid, which removes water: ethene.

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{excess conc. } H_2SO_4,\ 443\ K} CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2O}\)

(3) With ethanoic acid in the presence of an acid catalyst: an ester, ethyl ethanoate.

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH + CH_3COOH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\)

(4) With acidified potassium dichromate (oxidation): ethanoic acid.

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{acidified } K_2Cr_2O_7} CH_3COOH}\)

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem:
(i) Distinguish between hormonal co-ordination in plants and animals.

(ii) Which part of the brain is responsible for –

(1) intelligence

(2) riding a bicycle

(3) vomiting

(4) controlling hunger

(iii) How is brain and spinal-cord protected against mechanical injuries ?
rows.solution:
(i) Any two differences:

| Hormonal coordination in plants | Hormonal coordination in animals |
|---|---|
| Hormones reach the cells by simple diffusion | Hormones are carried by the blood to the target organ |
| No specialised glands are involved | Hormones are released by endocrine glands |

(ii) (1) Intelligence: the cerebrum (fore-brain).

(2) Riding a bicycle: the cerebellum (hind-brain).

(3) Vomiting: the medulla (hind-brain).

(4) Controlling hunger: the hypothalamus (fore-brain).

(iii) The brain sits inside a bony box, the skull (cranium), and inside it is held in a fluid-filled balloon that absorbs shocks. The spinal cord is protected by the backbone (vertebral column).

rows.stem:
(i) What are tropic movements ? Give an example of a plant hormone which (1) inhibits growth and (2) promotes cell division.

(ii) Explain directional movement of a tendril in pea plant in response to touch. Name the hormone responsible for this movement.
rows.solution:
(i) Tropic movements are directional growth movements of a plant in response to a stimulus such as light or gravity, towards it or away from it.

(1) A hormone that inhibits growth: abscisic acid.

(2) A hormone that promotes cell division: cytokinins.

(ii) When a tendril of the pea plant touches a support, auxin moves away from the point of contact. So the side of the tendril away from the support grows more than the side in contact with it. This unequal growth on the two sides makes the tendril coil around the support.

The hormone responsible is auxin.

rows.stem:
(a) Upper half of a convex lens is covered with a black paper. Draw a ray diagram to show the formation of image of an object placed at a distance of 2F from such a lens. Mention the position and nature of the image formed. State the observable difference in the image obtained if the lens is uncovered. Give reason to justify your answer.

(b) An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the optical centre of a concave lens of focal length 15 cm. Use lens formula to determine the distance of the image from the optical centre of the lens.
rows.solution:
(a) Covering the upper half of the lens does not stop the lower half from forming the image, so the ray diagram uses rays from the top of the object that pass through the uncovered lower half.

Ray diagram: draw the object at \(2\mathrm{F_1}\), with the upper half of the lens shaded black. From the top of the object draw a ray passing through \(\mathrm{F_1}\) to the lower half of the lens; after refraction it goes parallel to the principal axis. Draw a second ray from the top of the object through the optical centre, which goes straight on. The two meet below the axis at \(2\mathrm{F_2}\).

Position of the image: at \(2\mathrm{F_2}\), on the other side of the lens. Nature: real and inverted (and the same size as the object).

If the lens is uncovered, the image stays at the same position and has the same size and nature, but it becomes brighter. Reason: more rays from each point of the object pass through the lens and meet to form the image.

(b) For a concave lens, \(u = -30\) cm and \(f = -15\) cm. The lens formula gives

\(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{30} = -\dfrac{3}{30} = -\dfrac{1}{10}\).

So \(v = -10\) cm: the image is 10 cm from the optical centre, on the same side as the object (virtual and erect).

rows.stem: Identify the acid and base from which Sodium chloride is formed.
rows.context: Salts play a very important role in our daily life. Sodium chloride which is known as common salt is used almost in every kitchen. Baking soda is also a salt used in faster cooking as well as in baking industry. The family of salts is classified on the basis of cations and anions present in them.
rows.solution:
Sodium chloride is formed from hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH):

\(\mathrm{HCl + NaOH \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O}\)

rows.stem: Find the cation and the anion present in Calcium sulphate.
rows.context: Salts play a very important role in our daily life. Sodium chloride which is known as common salt is used almost in every kitchen. Baking soda is also a salt used in faster cooking as well as in baking industry. The family of salts is classified on the basis of cations and anions present in them.
rows.solution: In calcium sulphate, \(\mathrm{CaSO_4}\), the cation is the calcium ion, \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\), and the anion is the sulphate ion, \(\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}\).

rows.stem: “Sodium chloride and washing soda both belong to the same family of salts.” Justify this statement.
rows.context: Salts play a very important role in our daily life. Sodium chloride which is known as common salt is used almost in every kitchen. Baking soda is also a salt used in faster cooking as well as in baking industry. The family of salts is classified on the basis of cations and anions present in them.
rows.solution: Salts that have the same cation (or the same anion) belong to the same family. Sodium chloride (\(\mathrm{NaCl}\)) and washing soda (sodium carbonate, \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\)) both have the sodium ion, \(\mathrm{Na^+}\), as their cation, so both belong to the family of sodium salts, even though their anions differ.

rows.stem: Define the term pH scale. Name the salt obtained by the reaction of Potassium hydroxide and Sulphuric acid and give the pH value of its aqueous solution.
rows.context: Salts play a very important role in our daily life. Sodium chloride which is known as common salt is used almost in every kitchen. Baking soda is also a salt used in faster cooking as well as in baking industry. The family of salts is classified on the basis of cations and anions present in them.
rows.solution:
The pH scale is a scale for measuring the hydrogen ion (\(\mathrm{H^+}\)) concentration in a solution, usually from 0 (very acidic) to 14 (very basic).

Potassium hydroxide and sulphuric acid give potassium sulphate:

\(\mathrm{2KOH + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow K_2SO_4 + 2H_2O}\)

It is the salt of a strong acid and a strong base, so its aqueous solution is neutral, with pH 7.

rows.stem: Which of the cut pieces of the two Planaria could regenerate to form a complete organism ?
rows.context: Asexual reproduction involves a single parent to produce offsprings without the formation of gametes. It occurs by the following ways : Fission, Budding, Fragmentation, Spore formation and Regeneration. In one of the methods like regeneration, Planaria A is cut horizontally into three pieces – L, M and N and Planaria B is cut vertically into two equal halves – O and P.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the drawing shows Planaria A cut across into pieces L, M and N and Planaria B cut lengthwise into halves O and P; the passage states every piece and label, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 22.
rows.solution: All the cut pieces of both Planaria (L, M and N of Planaria A, and O and P of Planaria B) can regenerate to form a complete organism.

rows.stem: Give an example of another organism which follows the same mode of reproduction as Planaria.
rows.context: Asexual reproduction involves a single parent to produce offsprings without the formation of gametes. It occurs by the following ways : Fission, Budding, Fragmentation, Spore formation and Regeneration. In one of the methods like regeneration, Planaria A is cut horizontally into three pieces – L, M and N and Planaria B is cut vertically into two equal halves – O and P.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the drawing shows Planaria A cut across into pieces L, M and N and Planaria B cut lengthwise into halves O and P; the passage states every piece and label, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 22.
rows.solution: Hydra.

rows.stem: What is the meaning of ‘development’ in regeneration ?
rows.context: Asexual reproduction involves a single parent to produce offsprings without the formation of gametes. It occurs by the following ways : Fission, Budding, Fragmentation, Spore formation and Regeneration. In one of the methods like regeneration, Planaria A is cut horizontally into three pieces – L, M and N and Planaria B is cut vertically into two equal halves – O and P.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the drawing shows Planaria A cut across into pieces L, M and N and Planaria B cut lengthwise into halves O and P; the passage states every piece and label, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 22.
rows.solution: In regeneration, specialised cells of the cut piece proliferate and make a large number of cells. From this mass of cells, different cells undergo changes to become various cell types and tissues. These changes take place in an organised sequence, and this is called development.

rows.stem: Differentiate between regeneration and fragmentation.
rows.context: Asexual reproduction involves a single parent to produce offsprings without the formation of gametes. It occurs by the following ways : Fission, Budding, Fragmentation, Spore formation and Regeneration. In one of the methods like regeneration, Planaria A is cut horizontally into three pieces – L, M and N and Planaria B is cut vertically into two equal halves – O and P.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the drawing shows Planaria A cut across into pieces L, M and N and Planaria B cut lengthwise into halves O and P; the passage states every piece and label, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
| Regeneration | Fragmentation |
|---|---|
| Specialised cells of a cut body part proliferate to form new cells, which multiply and form a new individual | The body simply breaks up into pieces, and each piece grows by cell division into a new organism |
| Usually happens when the organism is cut or broken (for example Planaria, Hydra) | The organism breaks up naturally on maturing (for example Spirogyra) |

rows.stem: List two properties of heating elements.
rows.context: When electric current flows in a purely resistive circuit electrical energy gets fully converted into heat energy. The amount of heat produced (H) in the circuit is found to be directly proportional to (i) the square of current \((I^2)\) (ii) the resistance (R) of the conductor and (iii) the time (t) for which current flows. In other words \(H = I^2Rt\). Electrical devices such an electric fuse, electric heater, electric iron etc. are all based on this effect called heating effect of electric current.
rows.solution: Any two: heating elements are made of alloys with a higher resistivity than pure metals; they do not oxidise (burn) readily at high temperatures; they have a high melting point.

rows.stem: List two properties of electric fuse.
rows.context: When electric current flows in a purely resistive circuit electrical energy gets fully converted into heat energy. The amount of heat produced (H) in the circuit is found to be directly proportional to (i) the square of current \((I^2)\) (ii) the resistance (R) of the conductor and (iii) the time (t) for which current flows. In other words \(H = I^2Rt\). Electrical devices such an electric fuse, electric heater, electric iron etc. are all based on this effect called heating effect of electric current.
rows.solution: A fuse wire has a higher resistivity than pure metals, and it has a low melting point, so it melts quickly when the current becomes too large.

rows.stem: Name the principle on which an electric fuse works. Explain how a fuse wire is capable of saving electrical appliances from getting damaged due to accidently produced high currents.
rows.context: When electric current flows in a purely resistive circuit electrical energy gets fully converted into heat energy. The amount of heat produced (H) in the circuit is found to be directly proportional to (i) the square of current \((I^2)\) (ii) the resistance (R) of the conductor and (iii) the time (t) for which current flows. In other words \(H = I^2Rt\). Electrical devices such an electric fuse, electric heater, electric iron etc. are all based on this effect called heating effect of electric current.
rows.solution:
An electric fuse works on the heating effect of electric current.

The fuse wire is connected in series with the appliance. When an unduly high current flows by accident, the heat produced in the wire (\(H = I^2Rt\)) rises, the temperature of the wire goes above its low melting point, and it melts. This breaks the circuit and stops the current, so the appliance is saved from damage.

rows.stem: The power of an electric heater is 1100 W. If the potential difference between the two terminals of the heater is 220 V, find the current flowing in the circuit. What will happen to an electric fuse of rating 5 A connected in this circuit ?
rows.context: When electric current flows in a purely resistive circuit electrical energy gets fully converted into heat energy. The amount of heat produced (H) in the circuit is found to be directly proportional to (i) the square of current \((I^2)\) (ii) the resistance (R) of the conductor and (iii) the time (t) for which current flows. In other words \(H = I^2Rt\). Electrical devices such an electric fuse, electric heater, electric iron etc. are all based on this effect called heating effect of electric current.
rows.solution:
\(P = VI\), so \(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{1100}{220} = 5\) A.

A fuse melts only when the current through it exceeds its rating. Here the current is exactly 5 A, equal to the rating of the fuse, so the fuse does not melt and the heater works normally: there is no effect on the fuse. (The fuse has no margin to spare, though: any rise in the current above 5 A would melt it.)
